findings.reason: The normalized entire known133-character sentence merely expects a correct justified solution and supplies none. Equality is checked independently of task text, digits or subtask markers. No Goal-ID list, arbitrary length threshold, fuzzy classifier or new acceptance criterion was added. The925-row comparison identifies only the six actual Informatics instances in the observed catalog.

findings.reason: Nonmatching texts continue through the unchanged existing checks. Their passing is not proof of solvability, competence coverage, rubric adequacy, source fidelity or educational effectiveness. findings.subject: Actual graph and maturity/floor chain
findings.reason: The fixture gets a real complete ten-check passing integrity report from evaluateGraphIntegrity over an actual valid two-goal graph. The actual CQR202 aggregation and unchanged scope/curriculum/floor functions then show concrete-positive M4/M7 versus generic-negative M2/M3 and both M6/M7 floor failures with CQR202 diagnostics. Other rules are explicit passing fixture conditions; no real Informatics M0 masks the readiness failure and no current subject maturity approval is claimed.

findings.subject: Persistent exact negative fixtures and actual CI wiring
findings.reason: Fixtures retain the exact historical id/title/examData subset, including full task, solution, scoring and coverage. They are not a whole valid landscape and are not used as the graph input. Tests do not demand that current live tasks remain defective. The focused module is imported by the existing Deep CI entrypoint; two existing real Math/Physics tasks are positive controls,12 altered-task variants and8 existing guards stay negative.
